rationale: Record a Pulp-owned extension to the macOS window host's existing test-only pointer driver. PULP_TEST_POINTER_DRAG already accepted two fixed gesture shapes; it now also accepts an explicit rectangle form, rect:X0,Y0,X1,Y1,N[,R], which synthesises a straight drag between two points normalised to the content view with a top-left origin, in N steps emitting N+1 events, optionally repeated R times. This exists so an interaction can be driven deterministically from outside the process for measurement, replacing hand-timed gestures that cannot be reproduced across runs. The driver is reachable only when the environment variable is set, it synthesises the same mouseDown, mouseDragged and mouseUp calls the existing shapes already use, and it adds no new event source, no new rendering or backend path, and no production behavior. This changes no design ingest, no captured output, no rendering, layout or packaging behavior, no accepted expansion boundary, and no Vellum source authority.
